limitations: Exact historical verdict and stated assumptions only; migration makes no new scientific inference.

legacy.claim: A boost-violating model may produce an orientation-dependent split between in-plane lopsidedness and vertical displacement or warping
legacy.evidence: Moot: Branch C closed (ORB-11175). For the minimal equation the split does exist in form — the in-plane component of \(\mathbf{w}\) gives the tangential \(m=1\) force and the perpendicular component a midplane vertical acceleration falling as \(1/R\), a bowl-like differential forcing ([Branch C](branch-c.md) § The first-order moving-source solution) — but at amplitudes the ephemeris floor caps below \(10^{-3}\), so the disk-response derivation is no longer owed
legacy.kill: Moot: Branch C closed. Reopening needs an amplitude above the ephemeris ceiling.
